tiles.name: connect
tiles.doc: a .proto and a Connect server: Connect, gRPC and gRPC-Web on net/http

illegal_when.grpc-native: Connect speaks the gRPC protocol but is not grpc-go: its interceptors, reflection and health services do not plug in

satisfies.browser-clients: the Connect protocol is plain HTTP with JSON or binary bodies, so a browser calls it with no proxy
satisfies.streaming: a server-streaming RPC, over the Connect, gRPC and gRPC-Web protocols alike
satisfies.typed-clients: clients are generated from the .proto, in any language buf has a plugin for

cost_notes.llm-work: only validation and error mapping are left open
cost_notes.maintenance: a .proto and its generated code to keep in step, and field numbers that can never be reused

tiles.name: grpc
tiles.doc: a .proto and a grpc-go server

illegal_when.browser-clients: a browser cannot speak gRPC; it needs gRPC-Web and a proxy in front of the server

satisfies.grpc-native: it is grpc-go: interceptors, reflection, health and load balancing work as documented
satisfies.typed-clients: clients are generated from the .proto, in any language protoc has a plugin for

cost_notes.dependency: grpc-go and protobuf: a large module tree
cost_notes.llm-work: only validation and error mapping are left open
cost_notes.maintenance: a .proto and its generated code to keep in step, and field numbers that can never be reused

tiles.name: http-json
tiles.doc: net/http and JSON: a Handler and ServeMux over the package's stores

illegal_when.streaming: this tile generates request and response handlers only; a stream of events needs one of the schema tiles
illegal_when.typed-clients: there is no schema: every client writes its own requests and types by hand

satisfies.browser-clients: fetch and JSON, with nothing in between

cost_notes.dependency: net/http only; Go 1.22 routes methods and wildcards
cost_notes.llm-work: only validation and error mapping are left open

tiles.name: api-key
tiles.doc: a long-lived key per caller, resolved by a lookup you supply

illegal_when.expiring: a key is valid until someone deletes it; nothing in the credential says when to stop trusting it
illegal_when.offline-verify: a key carries no claims: every request is a lookup
illegal_when.third-party-idp: an API key is issued by you, not by an identity provider

satisfies.revocable: the key is resolved on every request, so removing it takes effect on the next one

cost_notes.llm-work: read a header and call the lookup; the store is the caller's
cost_notes.maintenance: keys are long-lived, so leaks are found late and rotation is manual

tiles.name: jwt-local
tiles.doc: a token this service signs and verifies itself, with no lookup

illegal_when.revocable: a signed token is valid until it expires; revoking one means a lookup on every request, which is the cost this scheme exists to avoid
illegal_when.third-party-idp: this issues its own tokens; it does not verify anyone else's

satisfies.expiring: the exp claim is inside the signed payload, so it cannot be altered
satisfies.offline-verify: the token carries its claims and its signature; verifying it touches nothing else

cost_notes.llm-work: parse a bearer header, verify a signature, check iss and exp
cost_notes.maintenance: the signing key has to be rotated, and rotation is a second key for a while
cost_notes.operations: a secret to distribute, nothing to run
cost_notes.runtime: one HMAC per request, no I/O

tiles.name: oidc
tiles.doc: an identity provider issues tokens; this verifies them against its keys

satisfies.expiring: the exp claim is inside the signed payload
satisfies.offline-verify: verification uses cached public keys, with no call per request
satisfies.revocable: the provider stops honouring a session, and short-lived tokens stop being reissued
satisfies.third-party-idp: this is the case it exists for: tokens are issued elsewhere and verified here

cost_notes.llm-work: verify with the provider's verifier, then map claims to a principal
cost_notes.operations: an identity provider to run or pay for, with clients, scopes and redirect URIs to keep right
cost_notes.runtime: keys are cached; a refresh is occasional

tiles.name: session-store
tiles.doc: an opaque session id in a cookie, looked up in a store on every request

illegal_when.offline-verify: the cookie carries an id and nothing else; there is nothing in it to verify without the store
illegal_when.third-party-idp: a session is issued here, after whatever login you run; it says nothing about who vouched for the user

satisfies.expiring: the stored session carries an expiry, checked on every read
satisfies.revocable: the session is read on every request, so deleting it takes effect on the next one

cost_notes.dependency: net/http cookies and a store the project already has
cost_notes.llm-work: read a cookie, load the session, check it has not expired
cost_notes.maintenance: expired sessions have to be swept, or the store grows forever
cost_notes.operations: nothing new to run: the sessions live in a store already chosen

tiles.name: kafka
tiles.doc: Kafka: a partitioned log, ordered per key, read back at will

illegal_when.no-broker: a cluster to run, partitions to size, and retention and consumer lag to watch

satisfies.at-least-once: an uncommitted offset is redelivered to whoever takes the partition next
satisfies.consumer-groups: a group shares partitions among its members and rebalances them
satisfies.cross-process: consumers in other processes read the topic over the network
satisfies.durable: a produce is acknowledged once the partition's replicas have the record
satisfies.fan-out: several consumer groups on one topic each see every record
satisfies.ordered: records with the same key go to one partition, and a partition is an ordered log
satisfies.replay: a consumer group can seek to any offset still inside retention

cost_notes.dependency: a client library with a large transitive graph
cost_notes.operations: the heaviest thing in the registry to run: brokers, partitions, rebalances, lag, and someone on call for them

tiles.name: local-bus
tiles.doc: in-process bus: synchronous delivery, ordered, errors joined

illegal_when.at-least-once: a handler that returns an error is not called again: the error is joined and returned to the publisher
illegal_when.consumer-groups: every handler is called for every event; there is no way to compete for one
illegal_when.cross-process: an in-process bus only reaches handlers in this program
illegal_when.durable: an in-process bus loses undelivered events on restart
illegal_when.replay: nothing is kept: a handler that subscribes later sees only what comes next

satisfies.fan-out: every subscriber is called for every event
satisfies.no-broker: a slice of handlers and a mutex; there is nothing to run
satisfies.ordered: Publish calls every handler in subscription order, in the publisher's goroutine

tiles.name: nats-core
tiles.doc: core NATS: subjects and queue groups, with nothing kept

illegal_when.at-least-once: core NATS delivers at most once and does not redeliver on failure
illegal_when.durable: core NATS is fire-and-forget: a message with no connected subscriber is gone
illegal_when.no-broker: there is a server to run, though only one binary and no state
illegal_when.replay: core NATS keeps no stream; there is nothing to read back

satisfies.consumer-groups: a queue group delivers each message to one of its members
satisfies.cross-process: subscribers in other processes receive what is published on a subject
satisfies.fan-out: every plain subscriber to a subject receives every message

unverified.ordered: messages from one publisher arrive in order on one connection, but nobody has checked what holds across a reconnect

cost_notes.llm-work: subscribe and publish on a subject; there is nothing to acknowledge
cost_notes.operations: one binary, no storage, nothing to size

tiles.name: nats-jetstream
tiles.doc: NATS JetStream: the same server with a log, so events are kept and can be read back

illegal_when.no-broker: a server to run, with streams and consumers to size and retain

satisfies.at-least-once: an unacknowledged message is redelivered until it is acknowledged or expires
satisfies.consumer-groups: a queue consumer shares its messages among its members
satisfies.cross-process: consumers in other processes read the stream over the network
satisfies.durable: a publish is acknowledged only once the stream has stored the message
satisfies.fan-out: several consumers on one stream each see every message
satisfies.ordered: a stream is an ordered log, and a consumer reads it in sequence
satisfies.replay: a consumer can start at any sequence or time in the stream

cost_notes.llm-work: publish with an ack, and a consumer with explicit acknowledgement
cost_notes.operations: one binary with no dependencies, but streams, consumers and retention to configure

tiles.name: rabbitmq
tiles.doc: RabbitMQ: exchanges, bindings and competing consumers

illegal_when.no-broker: a broker to run, and exchanges and bindings to get right
illegal_when.replay: a classic queue removes a message when it is acknowledged; there is nothing left to read back

satisfies.at-least-once: an unacknowledged message is requeued when the channel closes
satisfies.consumer-groups: several consumers on one queue compete for its messages
satisfies.cross-process: consumers in other processes bind to the exchange over the network
satisfies.fan-out: several queues bound to one exchange each receive every message

unverified.durable: a durable exchange, a durable queue and persistent messages are all needed, and this tile declares none of them
unverified.ordered: one consumer on one queue sees publisher order, but nobody has checked what requeueing does to it

cost_notes.operations: a broker to run, plus the topology to declare and keep in step

tiles.name: redis-streams
tiles.doc: Redis Streams: an append-only log with consumer groups

illegal_when.durable: durability is an operator setting: under the default append-only policy a second of writes can be lost on a crash
illegal_when.no-broker: there is a Redis to run

satisfies.at-least-once: an unacknowledged entry stays in the pending list and can be claimed again
satisfies.consumer-groups: a group shares entries among its consumers
satisfies.cross-process: clients in other processes read the stream over the network
satisfies.fan-out: several groups on one stream each see every entry
satisfies.ordered: one stream is an ordered sequence of ids
satisfies.replay: a stream is read from any id, so a late reader can start at the beginning

cost_notes.operations: one server, but stream trimming and group lag to watch

tiles.name: env-secrets
tiles.doc: environment variables, read once when the process starts

illegal_when.audited: nothing records which process read a variable, or when
illegal_when.rotating: a process's environment is fixed when it starts: a new value is not seen until a restart

cost_notes.operations: whatever starts the process already sets its environment

tiles.name: file-secrets
tiles.doc: one file per secret in a mounted directory, read on every call

illegal_when.audited: the file system does not record who read a file

satisfies.rotating: the file is read on every call, so a replaced file is seen at once

cost_notes.operations: something has to mount the directory: Kubernetes and Docker secrets do
cost_notes.runtime: a small file read per call

tiles.name: vault
tiles.doc: one path of a HashiCorp Vault KV v2 mount, read through a short cache

satisfies.audited: Vault's audit log records every read with the identity that made it
satisfies.rotating: a read is kept for a ttl you choose, so a new version is seen within it

cost_notes.dependency: the Vault API client and its module tree
cost_notes.maintenance: a client to keep logged in, and policies to keep in step with the paths
cost_notes.operations: a Vault to run, unseal, back up and upgrade
cost_notes.runtime: a network read when the cache expires

tiles.name: badger
tiles.doc: embedded key-value: an LSM store, one keyspace, values as JSON

illegal_when.cross-process: badger takes a directory lock; a second process cannot open the same store
illegal_when.lookup-by-field: one keyspace, one key; a secondary index would be written and repaired by hand

satisfies.durable: a directory on disk with a write-ahead log replayed on open
satisfies.no-broker: a library and a directory; there is no server

unverified.inbox: an inbox is one transaction over a handler's writes and the record that it ran; this tile does not generate one
unverified.outbox: an outbox is one transaction over the entity and the event; this tile does not generate one

cost_notes.dependency: badger and its own dependencies, but no server and no build-time tool
cost_notes.llm-work: id-keyed get, save and delete in one transaction; secondary indexes are excluded by illegal-when, not priced here
cost_notes.maintenance: no schema and no migrations: a field added to the struct changes stored values silently
cost_notes.runtime: an LSM tree with background compaction, unlike bbolt's single file

tiles.name: bolt
tiles.doc: embedded key-value: one file, a bucket per entity, values as JSON

illegal_when.cross-process: bbolt takes an exclusive lock on the file; a second process cannot open it
illegal_when.lookup-by-field: a bucket has one key; a secondary index would be written and repaired by hand

satisfies.durable: one memory-mapped file; a committed write transaction is fsynced before it returns
satisfies.no-broker: a file and a library; there is no server

unverified.inbox: an inbox is one transaction over a handler's writes and the record that it ran; this tile does not generate one
unverified.outbox: an outbox is one transaction over the entity and the event; this tile does not generate one

cost_notes.dependency: bbolt only, and no build-time tool
cost_notes.llm-work: every read, write and scan written by hand, including the key encoding
cost_notes.maintenance: no schema and no migrations: a field added to the struct changes stored documents silently, and nothing reports it

tiles.name: memory
tiles.doc: in-memory store: a map guarded by a mutex

illegal_when.cross-process: the map lives in this process's heap; another process has its own, empty one
illegal_when.durable: an in-memory map loses its data on restart
illegal_when.inbox: nothing is committed, so a handler's writes and the record that it ran cannot share a transaction
illegal_when.outbox: nothing is committed, so there is no transaction for an event to share

satisfies.lookup-by-field: a scan over the map: correct at any size, slow at a large one
satisfies.no-broker: a map and a mutex; there is nothing to run

tiles.name: mongo
tiles.doc: mongo: a collection per entity, documents rather than rows

illegal_when.no-broker: a mongo to run, with backups and a replica set for durability

satisfies.cross-process: a server other processes connect to over the network
satisfies.lookup-by-field: a filter on any field, and an index when you add one

unverified.durable: a write is durable only under a write concern and a replica set; the default is weaker, and this tile does not set it
unverified.inbox: a multi-document transaction needs a replica set, and this tile does not generate one
unverified.outbox: a multi-document transaction needs a replica set, and this tile does not generate one

cost_notes.dependency: the driver, and a server to run
cost_notes.llm-work: filters and updates written by hand, but no schema to keep in step
cost_notes.operations: a server to run, and a replica set if you want durable writes

tiles.name: postgres-pgx
tiles.doc: postgres via pgx: tilegen writes the schema, the LLM writes the SQL

illegal_when.no-broker: a postgres to run, with backups, connections and upgrades

satisfies.cross-process: a server other processes connect to over the network
satisfies.durable: a committed transaction is on disk before COMMIT returns
satisfies.lookup-by-field: a WHERE clause, and an index when you add one

unverified.inbox: an inbox is one transaction over a handler's writes and the record that it ran; this tile does not generate one
unverified.outbox: an outbox is one transaction over the entity and the event; this tile does not generate one

cost_notes.dependency: pgx only, and no build-time tool
cost_notes.llm-work: the LLM writes every query and scan by hand
cost_notes.maintenance: hand-written SQL drifts from the schema silently
cost_notes.operations: a server to run, with backups, connections and upgrades

tiles.name: postgres-sqlc
tiles.doc: postgres via sqlc: tilegen writes SQL, sqlc writes the Go, the LLM maps rows

illegal_when.no-broker: a postgres to run, with backups, connections and upgrades

satisfies.cross-process: a server other processes connect to over the network
satisfies.durable: a committed transaction is on disk before COMMIT returns
satisfies.inbox: a handler's writes and the record that it ran are committed in one transaction
satisfies.lookup-by-field: a WHERE clause, and an index when you add one
satisfies.outbox: the entity's row and the event's row are written in one transaction

cost_notes.dependency: pgx, plus sqlc as a build-time tool
cost_notes.llm-work: the LLM writes only row-to-domain mapping; sqlc writes the queries
cost_notes.operations: a server to run, plus sqlc in the build

tiles.name: sqlite-sqlc
tiles.doc: sqlite via sqlc: one file, no server; uuid and time are TEXT

illegal_when.cross-process: a sqlite file serves one process; another would need its own connection to the same disk

satisfies.durable: the database is a file on disk, and a committed transaction is in it
satisfies.lookup-by-field: a WHERE clause, and an index when you add one
satisfies.no-broker: one file and a library; there is no server

unverified.inbox: an inbox is one transaction over a handler's writes and the record that it ran; this tile does not generate one
unverified.outbox: an outbox is one transaction over the entity and the event; this tile does not generate one

cost_notes.dependency: a driver and sqlc, but no server to run
cost_notes.llm-work: same as postgres-sqlc: sqlc writes the queries

tiles.name: kafka
tiles.doc: Kafka as an inbound edge: consume a topic, at your own offset

illegal_when.no-broker: a cluster to run, partitions to size, and retention and consumer lag to watch

satisfies.at-least-once: an uncommitted offset is redelivered after a rebalance or a restart
satisfies.cross-process: the producers are other systems entirely; that is what an inbound edge is
satisfies.durable: a record is on the partition's replicas before it is acknowledged
satisfies.ordered: a partition is an ordered log, and one key goes to one partition
satisfies.replay: a consumer can start at any offset still inside retention

cost_notes.dependency: a client library with a large transitive graph
cost_notes.llm-work: a consumer group, offset commits after the handler, and a rebalance callback: more than the publish side
cost_notes.operations: the heaviest thing in the registry to run: brokers, partitions, rebalances, lag, and someone on call for them

tiles.name: nats-core
tiles.doc: core NATS: subjects and queue groups, with nothing kept

illegal_when.at-least-once: core NATS delivers at most once and does not redeliver on failure
illegal_when.durable: core NATS is fire-and-forget: a message with no connected consumer is gone
illegal_when.no-broker: there is a server to run, though only one binary and no state
illegal_when.replay: core NATS keeps no stream; JetStream is the same broker with a log

satisfies.cross-process: publishers in other processes reach this subject over the network

unverified.ordered: messages from one publisher arrive in order on one connection, but nobody has checked what holds across a reconnect

cost_notes.llm-work: subscribe to a subject and decode; there are no offsets to keep
cost_notes.operations: one binary, no storage, nothing to size

tiles.name: doc-mapper
tiles.doc: decodes mongo documents into domain types, by hand

tiles.name: row-mapper
tiles.doc: converts sqlc's row types to domain types, by hand
